The present writ petition has been filed with the prayer to issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari to quash the impugned revisional order dated 22.3.2021 passed by learned Sessions Judge, Sultanpur in Revision No. 42 of 2021 (Chhote Lal and others Vs. entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Judicial Magistrate, Sultanpur passed an order dated 26.7.2019 and summoned the petitioner no. 3,
Satyam Sharma under Sections 354, 323, 504, 506 IPC and petitioner nos. 1, 2, 4 and 5 under Sections 323, 504 and 506 IPC.
The petitioners challenged the said order by way of Criminal Revision No. 42 of 2021 which was rejected by the Sessions Judge, Sultanpur by its order dated 22.3.2021.
Aggrieved by the aforesaid orders, the petitioners have filed the present writ petition challenging the aforesaid orders.

At the very outset, learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that at present except petitioner no. 3, Satyam Sharma, all the other petitioners have been released on bail from trial court, therefore,
learned counsel for the petitioners does not want to press the prayer for quashing of the order dated 26.7.2019 passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-IInd, District Sultanpur in Criminal Case No. 393 of 2014 and the order dated 22.3.2021 passed by Sessions Judge, Sultanpur in Revision No.
42 of 2021 on their behalf, therefore, the writ petition may be dismissed on behalf of petitioner nos.
1, 2, 4 and 5.

Learned counsel has further submitted that he does not want to press the prayer for quashing of the aforesaid orders on behalf of petitioner no. 3 also as he has a good case of bail on the basis of parity.

He next submits that he is going to appear before the trial court to move the application for bail,
therefore, a direction to the subordinate court be given for expeditious disposal of bail application of the petitioner no. 3 keeping in mind the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, reported in (2021) 10 SCC 773.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, reported in (2021) 10 SCC 773
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA did not oppose the prayer made by learned counsel for the petitioners for not pressing the present petition on behalf of the petitioners.
In view of above, the present petition is hereby dismissed as not pressed.

However, trial court is directed that if the petitioner no. 3, Satyam Sharma appears before trial court and moves his bail application within three weeks from today before the court concerned, the bail application shall be decided expeditiously in accordance with law keeping in mind the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, reported in (2021) 10 SCC 773.
